newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say Kinshasa to fall by end-June.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say Kinshasa to fall by end-June.

text.p: Zairean rebels said on Monday they would take the capital Kinshasa by the end of June after less than nine months of fighting against the government of President Mobutu Sese Seko.
"The capital Kinshasa will fall by the end of June," rebel radio Voice of the People said, quoting rebel leader Laurent Kabila in the eastern border town of Goma.

Rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation Congo/Zaire (AFDL) control most of the more populous eastern half of the vast country after taking the diamond-capital Mbuji-Mayi on Friday.
But Kinshasa is more than 950 km (594 miles) west of Mbuji-Mayi and 1,040 km (650 miles) southwest of the third largest city of Kisangani, which fell on March 15.
The rebels are advancing towards the second city Lubumbashi, capital of Shaba region. Rebel sources have suggested Lubumbashi will fall this week.
Hundreds of kilometres (miles) of forest and a series of towns including Kananga and Kikwet in the southwest and Basanku, Mbandaka and Bandundu on the Zaire river separate the rebels from Kinshasa.
Privately alliance officials say they expected the campaign which started last October to last years and concede military logistics hampered their advance more than resistance from the Zaire army.

Peace talks in South Africa led by U.N. Special Envoy to the Great Lakes region Mohamed Sahnoun aimed at agreeing a ceasefire and organising a summit between President Mobutu Sese Seko and Kabila entered a third day on Monday.
